citation: Real-estate column, Chicago Daily Tribune, 8 November 1903: the building news that Thompson-Reid and Collins Bros. 'have begun the construction of a four story building ... and a barn, at 1605 to 1618 [1613] Indiana avenue'.
author: Chicago Daily Tribune
locator: The real-estate column's building news: '[Thompson]-Reid and Collins Bros., manufacturers of ice cream, have begun the construction of a four story building to be occupied for the manufacture of ice cream, and a barn, at 1605 to 1618 [1613] Indiana avenue, the cost of which will be $50,000. The building will front 100 feet, with a depth of 177, and will be of brick. The plans were prepared by A. R. Buckley.' The OCR reads the number '1618'; the September sale and the March 1904 report both give 1605-1613.
rights_note: A US newspaper published in 1903, in the public domain. Read for a building's storeys, material, size and start.
access_notes: Found 2026-10-25 (T-3130) through the Internet Archive's full-text search of the Tribune for "Collins Bros" "ice cream"; read from the item's OCR text.
note: The building the plant was to be: four storeys of brick, 100 by 177 feet, with a barn, $50,000, from A. R. Buckley's plans. 'Have begun' is the column's word in November 1903, but the foundation was still being dug on 22 March 1904 (abendpost_1904_03_22_indiana_1605_foundation), so the start the column reports is not the walls' start.
what_it_supplies: the plant's planned form: a four-storey brick building 100 by 177 feet, with a barn
its architect, A. R. Buckley, and its cost, $50,000
what_it_does_not_supply: how far the walls had risen by 1 July 1904
